chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

When a man had learned a Surah (of the Holy Quran) and then forgot it or neglected it, and he enters Paradise, it will appear to him from above in the most beautiful form, saying: 'Do you recognise me?' He will say, 'No.' It will say: 'I am Surah such and such. You did not act by me and you abandoned me. But by God, had you acted by me, I would have made you reach this rank.' And it gestured with its hand to what was above it.

key_terms.أشرفت عليه: Ashrafa 'alayhi — appeared over him, looked down upon him from above; signals a higher vantage point
key_terms.الدرجة: Al-daraja — rank or level in Paradise; Islamic theology holds Paradise to have multiple tiers of reward corresponding to deeds
key_terms.السورة: Surah — a chapter of the Quran; here personified as a sentient being in the afterlife
key_terms.تركتني: Taraktani — you abandoned/neglected me; implies moral failure to live by Quranic teachings

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who forgets or neglects a Surah of the Quran in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith narrated by Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) presents a vivid eschatological scene in which Quranic surahs take on personified forms in Paradise. The Imam teaches that a Surah which was learned but not acted upon will appear to its former learner in a beautiful form, lamenting that neglect of its teachings prevented that person from attaining higher ranks. This reflects the early Shia theological principle that the Quran is not merely recited but must be internalized and practiced, and that different ranks in Paradise are tied to one's engagement with and practice of Quranic teachings.
word_analysis: I would have made you reach
